highlights.content: ![](/images/investing-live-logo.svg) ![](/images/investing-live-logo.svg) # Morgan Stanley says it's time to look beyond chips as AI benefits spread to Airbnb, Home Depot and more ## Summary ![](https://investinglive.com/cms/media/Processed/Categories/featured/Have some Coke 25 September 2026-featured-1790292128.jpg?width=768&format=webp) The note gives investors a reason to rotate, not to sell: the money moving out of crowded AI hardware positions would go to software and non-tech adopters, not out of the AI theme altogether. That could support a broadening of US equity gains beyond the megacaps. The weakest point in the argument is the scarcity thesis for hardware, which rests on bottlenecks like energy shortages and politics that could ease or tighten quickly. Regulation risk now sits alongside those bottlenecks. [Tuesday's White House meeting](/stocks/trump-johnson-to-meet-tech-ceos-on-ai-september-29-as-pressure-to-regulate-builds/) with tech CEOs on AI is a near-term test. Adopters and infrastructure software look less exposed to any rules on frontier models than the model builders whose spending drives chip demand. --- Morgan Stanley's advice is to keep the AI hardware winners but stop relying on them alone. Scarcity should keep chips profitable for longer, while the next gains come from companies actually putting AI to work. **Summary:** Morgan Stanley is urging investors to take a "barbell" approach to artificial intelligence, [MarketWatch](https://www.marketwatch.com/story/heres-how-to-position-your-portfolio-for-the-next-ai-wave-according-to-morgan-stanley-ac8f8a4a) reported. That means holding on to the chipmakers and infrastructure names at the core of the build-out, while branching into a broader set of companies that are starting to see real gains from the technology. The recommendation came in a Thursday note from a team of analysts led by Stephen Byrd. On one side of the barbell sit the AI enablers. Chip and infrastructure stocks have broadly outperformed the S&P 500 since the AI wave began. The analysts still see room for further gains, although they advise being selective to free up space for new ideas. Semiconductor analyst Joe Moore said demand from data-centre customers remains exceptionally strong. He named Nvidia and Broadcom among his preferred picks, on the back of spending by AI model developers. The team expects demand for computing power to outstrip supply for years. In earlier technology cycles, market leadership typically rotated from one sector to the next as a trend matured. This time, the analysts argue, the build-out has been slowed by local backlash, energy shortages and politics. That should keep hardware scarce and give its suppliers a longer window to profit. On the other side of the barbell are early software enablers and AI adopters, and the analysts say now is the time to start adding exposure to them. In software, analyst Adam Wood favours infrastructure names including Microsoft, Snowflake, Datadog, Cloudflare and Dynatrace. These companies provide the underlying systems on which AI applications run. Beyond technology, the note points to new AI entrants across healthcare, real estate, autos and consumer services. The analysts argue that the rapid scaling of large language model capabilities points to a broad opportunity for value creation. They highlight companies that are putting numbers on the benefits: The bank also holds positive ratings on a range of adopters in more traditional industries, including Home Depot, Procter and Gamble, GE Aerospace and Coca-Cola. Transportation and real estate are also flagged as sectors to watch. The call comes as investors weigh how long the concentrated rally in AI hardware can run. By arguing that enablers and adopters can both work, Morgan Stanley is offering a way to stay with the AI theme while spreading bets more widely across the market. ![Stanley_id_c09734a1-1e1d-4191-b6fe-c832db2218fe_original.jpg](https://investinglive.com/cms/media/imag...

highlights.content: [Skip to content](#main) [![Tech Edition](/wp-content/themes/tech-edition/assets/images/logo.svg)](https://www.techedt.com/) [AI](/tag/ai)[Cybersecurity](/tag/cybersecurity)[Data Centres](/tag/data-centres)[Start-ups](/tag/startups)[NVIDIA](/tag/nvidia) [Home](https://www.techedt.com/)/[Business](https://www.techedt.com/category/business) Business # ASUS expands NVIDIA-based AI systems across data centres, desktops and edge computing At NVIDIA AI Day Singapore 2026, ASUS unveiled Rubin and Blackwell systems engineered for enterprise training, deskside computing and industrial automation. ![Nurin Sofia](https://techedt.gumlet.io/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/Nurin-Sofia.jpg?compress=true) **[Nurin Sofia](https://www.techedt.com/author/nurin-sofia)**24 September 2026 · 3 min read [![](https://www.techedt.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/google.svg)Add as a preferred **source on Google**](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=techedt.com)[![](/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/news.svg)Follow us on **Google News**](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAqJQgKIh9DQklTRVFnTWFnMEtDM1JsWTJobFpIUXVZMjl0S0FBUAE?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen) ![ASUS expands NVIDIA-based AI systems across data centres, desktops and edge computing](https://www.techedt.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/ASUS-expands-NVIDIA-based-AI-systems-across-data-centres-desktops-and-edge-computing-1440x810.jpg) At NVIDIA AI Day Singapore 2026, ASUS detailed a range of NVIDIA-powered AI systems spanning rack-scale infrastructure, desktop systems, edge computing and storage. Across these categories, the portfolio supports workloads including model training, inference, agentic AI and industrial automation. For its larger data centre platforms, ASUS is using NVIDIA Vera Rubin and HGX Rubin architectures. Smaller systems complement these platforms for local model development and inference. ## Rubin systems address high-density AI workloads Built for rack-scale deployments, the ASUS AI POD XA VR721-E3 is based on the NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 platform. ASUS claims that the system delivers up to 10 times the performance per watt of the previous generation, targeting high-volume AI processing and lower-cost token generation. For training, inference and post-training workloads, the XA NR1I-E12LR and XA NR1I-E12L use NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8. To meet the performance and efficiency requirements of high-density data centres, the XA NR1I-E12L Series supports liquid or hybrid cooling configurations. Agentic AI workloads are addressed by the XA P2N-E2, a 2U NVIDIA MGX platform equipped with two NVIDIA Vera CPUs and support for up to two dual-slot NVIDIA GPUs. ASUS designed the system for AI reasoning, data processing and orchestration at scale. ## Desktop systems support local AI development The ExpertCenter Pro ET900N G3 brings large-model development and inference into a deskside system. Built on NVIDIA DGX Station architecture, it uses the GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip and provides up to 20 PFLOPS of AI performance with 748GB of coherent CPU-GPU memory. The smaller ASUS Ascent GX10 is based on NVIDIA DGX Spark and uses the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip, delivering up to 1 petaFLOP of AI performance with 128GB of unified memory in a 150 x 150 x 51 mm chassis for local model development, fine-tuning and inference. Support for NVIDIA ConnectX-7 also allows two GX10 systems to work together on larger AI models. ProArt GR1X targets creators, developers and professionals working on Windows. Powered by NVIDIA RTX Spark, the workstation combines a 20-core NVIDIA Grace CPU with a Blackwell RTX GPU, up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 1 petaFLOP of FP4 AI performance. ASUS lists always-on local AI agents, creative workloads, AI development and advanced 3D work among its intended uses. ## Edge systems extend AI processing into industrial environments The ESC8000-E12P supports NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 and RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs for enterprise inference, vision AI and vis...

Just before he took the stage, Auth0 chief product officer, Gareth Davies, told me why he thinks identity now belongs on the revenue line. Some retailers, merchants and travel companies are now watching between 10% and 40% of their traditional Google search traffic go somewhere else entirely: to AI agents. "Think about that for a second. It's pretty existential," [Auth0](https://auth0.com/) chief product officer, [Gareth Davies](https://www.linkedin.com/in/garethjamesdavies/), told me at [Oktane 2026](https://www.okta.com/oktane/) in Las Vegas. Shoppers now hand their intent to ChatGPT or Gemini and have a proper conversation about what they want. If a brand isn't in that conversation, Davies said, "you're kind of out of the equation, and you're very likely to miss a sale." The upside is why Auth0 is so keen. Davies said brands that do meet shoppers inside agents "typically convert those users at three to five times greater than their traditional traffic." (I'd treat that as a best case. [Adobe's data](https://business.adobe.com/blog/ai-driven-traffic-surges-across-industries) for the 2025 US holiday season had AI-referred retail traffic up 693% year on year and converting 31% better than other traffic. That's impressive, and still a long way short of three times, although with AI moving so fast, my observation could be out of date by the time this article is printed.) [Okta](https://www.okta.com/) bought Auth0 in 2021 in a deal worth about [US$6.5 billion](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20210503005412/en/Okta-Completes-Acquisition-of-Auth0), and it now runs as Okta's customer identity platform. I sat down with Davies the day before he opened the Auth0 keynote on Wednesday 23 September, a few hours after [Okta](https://www.okta.com/) co-founder and CEO, [Todd McKinnon](https://www.linkedin.com/in/toddmckinnon/), laid out his [blueprint for the secure agentic enterprise](https://itwire.com/business-it-news/data/okta-wants-every-ai-agent-to-carry-id-and-australias-medicare-breach-just-made-the-case-for-it). Davies' message was the same in our chat and on stage. "Identity is now a board-level discussion," he said. ***You can watch the full Auth0 keynote below, please watch and read on!*** **Identity moves onto the revenue line** Davies said he's spent the past 12 months talking with big consumer brands and B2B software makers. Those talks now centre on customer acquisition, lifetime value and fraud reduction. He also sees identity settling an old fight between the CISO, who wants security, and the chief digital officer, who wants frictionless sign-ups. "Once you see this, it cannot be unseen," Davies said. His showcase was [Dine Brands](https://www.dinebrands.com/), owner of Applebee's and IHOP (his kids' favourite, he admitted). Davies said Dine Brands used Auth0 to lift the guest loyalty experience in its app, and saw a 15% increase in order value through its AI commerce channels while account takeover and loyalty abuse fraud fell by more than 95%. (Photo by ANGELA WEISS / AFP)](/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/afp_6ab4da0c8541-1790237196.jpg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80) OpenAI CEO Sam Altman arrives to attend a Security Council meeting on AI, at the UN headquarters in New York, US, September 23, 2026 [Angela Weiss/AFP] [![](/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/2017-06-08T131939Z_1189275883_RC11B0FE7F20_RTRMADP_3_GULF-QATAR-JAZEERA-1714943623.jpg?resize=96%2C96&quality=80)](/author/al_jazeera_staff_150119130629458) By [Al Jazeera Staff](/author/al_jazeera_staff_150119130629458) Published On 24 Sep 202624 Sep 2026 Australian authorities have raised the alarm after OpenAI-powered models hacked into a government health data system in June, slipping past its digital defences and accessing files without authorisation. This is the first publicly known case of artificial intelligence (AI) “agents” – AI-powered software systems that can carry out tasks autonomously – breaking into a government website, and the latest of several AI breaches of external systems. ## Recommended Stories list of 3 items * list 1 of 3[As AI leaders warn of catastrophe, US and China shun slowdown calls](/economy/2026/9/23/as-ai-leaders-warn-of-catastrophe-us-and-china-shun-slowdown-calls) * list 2 of 3[What’s the US–China AI ‘hotline’ that Trump plans to pitch to Xi Jinping?](/news/2026/9/21/whats-the-us-china-ai-hotline-that-trump-plans-to-pitch-to-xi) * list 3 of 3[US lawmakers propose sweeping AI restrictions with superintelligence ban](/economy/2026/9/23/us-lawmakers-propose-sweeping-ai-restrictions-with-superintelligence-ban) end of list The disclosure comes as top AI firms [warn of the risk](/economy/2026/9/11/us-legislators-push-ai-safety-laws-amid-human-extinction-warnings) of humans losing control of AI, calling for its development to slow to a pace that allows it to be safely regulated. Global powers must cooperate to ensure this, they have said. A research scientist at AI firm Anthropic, Evan Hubinger, went so far as to say he believes there is a greater than 10 percent chance AI could “kill all humans” within a decade. Addressing the United Nations Security Council on Wednesday, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said [there is a risk](/video/newsfeed/2026/9/24/openai-ceo-tech-companies-dont-have-all-the-answers-on-ai-policy) of AI moving “so fast that people can no longer follow what’s happening or intervene when needed”. “This would obviously be terrible,” he said. “And we should not train models that we cannot make an extremely strong case that we will be able to keep under human control.” ## What do we know about the AI breach in Australia? Advertisement When OpenAI accessed the government portal while conducting research on public medical spending, Albanese said the AI agent circumvented “blocks” that should have prevented it from breaking into the portal. “The AI agent found a way around those blocks – didn’t accept no for an answer,” said Albanese. Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles said the information the OpenAI agent accessed was “not particularly sensitive” and was later publicly released. Still, Albanese called the situation “obviously unacceptable” and said Australia had relayed its “extreme concern” to OpenAI,...

With the theme **Turn Your Intents into Business Outcomes**, WOW 2026 marked a defining moment for the enterprise AI landscape. Workato's neutral control and execution platform for enterprise AI and AIRO (a multi-agent system that brings agentic engineering to the enterprise) is changing the way businesses orchestrate their processes and govern AI execution at scale. Customers Lenovo, VOIS (Vodafone Intelligent Solutions), and Red Hat shared how they're putting orchestration and governance to work in their own use of AI: AI providers Anthropic, OpenAI, and Amazon Web Services (AWS) explained how pairing models with a control and execution platform can help customers drive more value with AI: Attendees also heard from Workato’s vibrant global partner community and ecosystem leaders and explored co-innovations from companies like Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, UST, Workday, and Reltio. Southeast Asia’s AI compute race is set to add 22,000 more Blackwell Ultra GPUs. Singapore-founded AI cloud provider Aolani said Sept. 21 that it plans to deploy 22,000 Nvidia Blackwell Ultra GPUs across two AI factories in Malaysia and the Philippines in early 2027. The expansion would take Aolani’s total GPU deployment above 48,000 and its AI factory capacity past 100 MW. highlights.content: [![Quartz](https://static.qz.com/quartz-v1.128.0/_next/static/media/quartz-logo.1poxn91047rb6.svg?dpl=n5st3rj5gqpn)](/) [A.I.](/tech-innovation/ai) # An OpenAI agent hacked Australia's Medicare portal, and the country's PM is furious Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said OpenAI took nearly 3 months to notify Canberra about the June breach [By Cris Tolomia](/author/cristolomia)·2 min read·Updated September 24, 2026 [Add QZ to Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=qz.com) SOPA Images / Getty Images Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said an OpenAI agent [gained unauthorized access](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-23/openai-agent-hacked-australian-government-website-albanese-says) to the country's Medicare Statistics Reporting Service portal on June 18, marking what cybersecurity researchers are calling the first known instance of an AI model breaching a government database without direction from a malicious actor. The portal, administered by Services Australia, contains non-sensitive Medicare information including spending statistics. Albanese said the agent retrieved both public and non-public files from the portal, and that there is no current indication that any personal information was exposed. A forensic investigation aided by the Australian Signals Directorate is underway. According to OpenAI, the incident arose from an internal evaluation exercise where its models were tasked with finding information and statistics related to Australia. "In the course of that, our models took actions we did not intend," an OpenAI spokesperson told [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/24/openai-agent-hacked-australian-government-website-.html). The company said it did not become aware of the June breach until August, when it was conducting a review of what it calls "misaligned model activity," and notified Services Australia on Sept. 10. Albanese, speaking on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Thursday, said he had spoken directly with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman to express Australia's "extreme concern" over the incident and criticized the three-month delay in notification. "Mr. Altman certainly has acknowledged — and I've invited further discussions with him as well — that their protocols were not up to scratch here," Albanese said. Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles called the intrusion "utterly unacceptable" and described it as "a warning about the technology being developed without safeguards and without guardrails in place," according to Bloomberg. According to [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/09/24/openai-agents-australia-data-breach), the country plans to stand up a multi-agency cyber task force that will examine the breach, weigh potential legislative changes, and decide whether to refer the case to federal police. The Medicare breach was part of a broader pattern of behavior. AI safety firm Transluce determined that OpenAI agents had also tried to reach several websites during May and June, among them a digital library run by the University of New Mexico and Data USA, a government-data aggregation platform, Bloomberg reported. The model tried to access four Australian state and federal government websites requesting data but successfully breached only one, Marles said. Thursday's disclosure came as OpenAI faces widening scrutiny over its agents' autonomous behavior. The company [published a technical report in August](https://qz.com/openai-technical-report-ai-agents-hacked-hugging-face-082726) detailing how its models escaped a controlled testing environment in July and compromised parts of AI platform Hugging Face's production infrastructure, accessing credentials and private code repositories. Just before he took the stage, Auth0 chief product officer, Gareth Davies, told me why he thinks identity now belongs on the revenue line. Some retailers, merchants and travel companies are now watching between 10% and 40% of their traditional Google search traffic go somewhere else entirely: to AI agents. "Think about that for a second. It's pretty existential," [Auth0](https://auth0.com/) chief product officer, [Gareth Davies](https://www.linkedin.com/in/garethjamesdavies/), told me at [Oktane 2026](https://www.okta.com/oktane/) in Las Vegas. Shoppers now hand their intent to ChatGPT or Gemini and have a proper conversation about what they want. If a brand isn't in that conversation, Davies said, "you're kind of out of the equation, and you're very likely to miss a sale." The upside is why Auth0 is so keen. Davies said brands that do meet shoppers inside agents "typically convert those users at three to five times greater than their traditional traffic." (I'd treat that as a best case. [Adobe's data](https://business.adobe.com/blog/ai-driven-traffic-surges-across-industries) for the 2025 US holiday season had AI-referred retail traffic up 693% year on year and converting 31% better than other traffic. That's impressive, and still a long way short of three times, although with AI moving so fast, my observation could be out of date by the time this article is printed.) [Okta](https://www.okta.com/) bought Auth0 in 2021 in a deal worth about [US$6.5 billion](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20210503005412/en/Okta-Completes-Acquisition-of-Auth0), and it now runs as Okta's customer identity platform. I sat down with Davies the day before he opened the Auth0 keynote on Wednesday 23 September, a few hours after [Okta](https://www.okta.com/) co-founder and CEO, [Todd McKinnon](https://www.linkedin.com/in/toddmckinnon/), laid out his [blueprint for the secure agentic enterprise](https://itwire.com/business-it-news/data/okta-wants-every-ai-agent-to-carry-id-and-australias-medicare-breach-just-made-the-case-for-it). Davies' message was the same in our chat and on stage. "Identity is now a board-level discussion," he said. ***You can watch the full Auth0 keynote below, please watch and read on!*** **Identity moves onto the revenue line** Davies said he's spent the past 12 months talking with big consumer brands and B2B software makers. AI Agents.content: [Live](/video/live) [Live](/video/live) EXPLAINER [News](/news/)|[Technology](/tag/technology/) # How an OpenAI ‘agent’ hacked Australia’s Medicare and what that means *Incident highlights growing concerns about AI’s impact on cybersecurity and AI disclosure procedures, say experts.* Save Share ![OpenAI CEO Sam Altman arrives to attend a UN Security Council meeting on Artificial Intelligence during the 81st United Nations General Assembly at UN headquarters in New York on September 23, 2026. (Photo by ANGELA WEISS / AFP)](/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/afp_6ab4da0c8541-1790237196.jpg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80) OpenAI CEO Sam Altman arrives to attend a Security Council meeting on AI, at the UN headquarters in New York, US, September 23, 2026 [Angela Weiss/AFP] [![](/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/2017-06-08T131939Z_1189275883_RC11B0FE7F20_RTRMADP_3_GULF-QATAR-JAZEERA-1714943623.jpg?resize=96%2C96&quality=80)](/author/al_jazeera_staff_150119130629458) By [Al Jazeera Staff](/author/al_jazeera_staff_150119130629458) Published On 24 Sep 202624 Sep 2026 Australian authorities have raised the alarm after OpenAI-powered models hacked into a government health data system in June, slipping past its digital defences and accessing files without authorisation. This is the first publicly known case of artificial intelligence (AI) “agents” – AI-powered software systems that can carry out tasks autonomously – breaking into a government website, and the latest of several AI breaches of external systems. ## Recommended Stories list of 3 items * list 1 of 3[As AI leaders warn of catastrophe, US and China shun slowdown calls](/economy/2026/9/23/as-ai-leaders-warn-of-catastrophe-us-and-china-shun-slowdown-calls) * list 2 of 3[What’s the US–China AI ‘hotline’ that Trump plans to pitch to Xi Jinping?](/news/2026/9/21/whats-the-us-china-ai-hotline-that-trump-plans-to-pitch-to-xi) * list 3 of 3[US lawmakers propose sweeping AI restrictions with superintelligence ban](/economy/2026/9/23/us-lawmakers-propose-sweeping-ai-restrictions-with-superintelligence-ban) end of list The disclosure comes as top AI firms [warn of the risk](/economy/2026/9/11/us-legislators-push-ai-safety-laws-amid-human-extinction-warnings) of humans losing control of AI, calling for its development to slow to a pace that allows it to be safely regulated. Global powers must cooperate to ensure this, they have said. A research scientist at AI firm Anthropic, Evan Hubinger, went so far as to say he believes there is a greater than 10 percent chance AI could “kill all humans” within a decade. Addressing the United Nations Security Council on Wednesday, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said [there is a risk](/video/newsfeed/2026/9/24/openai-ceo-tech-companies-dont-have-all-the-answers-on-ai-policy) of AI moving “so fast that people can no longer follow what’s happening or intervene when needed”. “This would obviously be terrible,” he said. “And we should not train models that we cannot make an extremely strong case that we will be able to keep under human control.” ## What do we know about the AI breach in Australia? Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese [revealed the breach on Wednesday](/news/2026/9/24/australia-says-openai-agent-hacked-medicare-portal), saying an OpenAI agent had made its way into the public-facing medical statistics portal of Medicare, the country’s universal health insurance system, on July 18. PallasAI Insights allows teams to move from the total score to the response detail behind it. A single blended score may hide a strong result in ChatGPT and a weak result in Perplexity, while a topic heatmap can reveal customer questions for which the brand is rarely or never recommended. Audit and monitoring findings can be sent into an opportunity map that organizes the affected topics and prepares work for the Agent. AI Agents.content: [![Quartz](https://static.qz.com/quartz-v1.128.0/_next/static/media/quartz-logo.1poxn91047rb6.svg?dpl=n5st3rj5gqpn)](/) [A.I.](/tech-innovation/ai) # An OpenAI agent hacked Australia's Medicare portal, and the country's PM is furious Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said OpenAI took nearly 3 months to notify Canberra about the June breach [By Cris Tolomia](/author/cristolomia)·2 min read·Updated September 24, 2026 [Add QZ to Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=qz.com) SOPA Images / Getty Images Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said an OpenAI agent [gained unauthorized access](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-23/openai-agent-hacked-australian-government-website-albanese-says) to the country's Medicare Statistics Reporting Service portal on June 18, marking what cybersecurity researchers are calling the first known instance of an AI model breaching a government database without direction from a malicious actor. The portal, administered by Services Australia, contains non-sensitive Medicare information including spending statistics. Albanese said the agent retrieved both public and non-public files from the portal, and that there is no current indication that any personal information was exposed. A forensic investigation aided by the Australian Signals Directorate is underway. According to OpenAI, the incident arose from an internal evaluation exercise where its models were tasked with finding information and statistics related to Australia. "In the course of that, our models took actions we did not intend," an OpenAI spokesperson told [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/24/openai-agent-hacked-australian-government-website-.html). The company said it did not become aware of the June breach until August, when it was conducting a review of what it calls "misaligned model activity," and notified Services Australia on Sept. 10. Albanese, speaking on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Thursday, said he had spoken directly with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman to express Australia's "extreme concern" over the incident and criticized the three-month delay in notification. "Mr. Altman certainly has acknowledged — and I've invited further discussions with him as well — that their protocols were not up to scratch here," Albanese said. Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles called the intrusion "utterly unacceptable" and described it as "a warning about the technology being developed without safeguards and without guardrails in place," according to Bloomberg. According to [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/09/24/openai-agents-australia-data-breach), the country plans to stand up a multi-agency cyber task force that will examine the breach, weigh potential legislative changes, and decide whether to refer the case to federal police. The Medicare breach was part of a broader pattern of behavior. AI safety firm Transluce determined that OpenAI agents had also tried to reach several websites during May and June, among them a digital library run by the University of New Mexico and Data USA, a government-data aggregation platform, Bloomberg reported. The model tried to access four Australian state and federal government websites requesting data but successfully breached only one, Marles said. Thursday's disclosure came as OpenAI faces widening scrutiny over its agents' autonomous behavior. The company [published a technical report in August](https://qz.com/openai-technical-report-ai-agents-hacked-hugging-face-082726) detailing how its models escaped a controlled testing environment in July and compromised parts of AI platform Hugging Face's production infrastructure, accessing credentials and private code repositories. AI Agents.title: Dataiku debuts cross-platform Agent Management, expands Cobuild building agent - SiliconANGLE
AI Agents.titleZh: Dataiku debuts cross-platform Agent Management, expands Cobuild building agent - SiliconANGLE
AI Agents.content: UPDATED 09:00 EDT / SEPTEMBER 24 2026 ### Dataiku debuts cross-platform Agent Management, expands Cobuild building agent by Duncan Riley Enterprise artificial intelligence platform company Dataiku Inc. today launched Agent Management, a standalone product that finds and tracks every AI agent a business runs, including those built on other vendors’ platforms. Dataiku also expanded Cobuild, its natural-language agent for building AI projects. Agent Management is aimed at a gap in how large companies keep track of what they run. Most maintain a record of who owns each piece of software and when its license renews, and Dataiku argues that almost none can produce the same for their agents. Fewer than one in five organizations keep a complete and current inventory of their AI systems, according to research from IBM Corp. cited by the company. A bank can say how many servers it runs “to the decimal,” said Florian Douetteau, co-founder and chief executive of Dataiku. Ask the same bank about its AI agents and the answer is “a shrug or a guess,” he said. Once connected to the platforms where a company’s agents run, the software pulls them into a single inventory. Connectors cover Salesforce Inc.’s Agentforce and the agent services run by Amazon Web Services Inc., Microsoft Corp. and Google LLC. Agents built on Databricks Inc. or Snowflake Inc. show up too, as do Dataiku’s own, and custom environments can report in through the OpenTelemetry standard. Each entry maps the tools and models an agent depends on so supervisors can see how it works. The riskiest agents carry a standing record of certification status and named risks. Tests on them rerun on a schedule, so an evidence trail is already in place when an auditor or regulator asks for one. Dataiku is positioning the product against monitoring tools built into a single vendor’s stack, which it argues tend to favor that vendor’s own agents. Sitting above every vendor’s stack lets Agent Management answer portfolio-wide questions, such as where risk is concentrated or which agents cost more than they return. Users can pose those questions in plain language. Plain-language questions are also at the center of the Cobuild update. Dataiku made Cobuild generally available in June as an agent that turns a business request into a governed Dataiku project without code, and the expansion carries that approach across the platform. A new feature called Cobuild Insights lets any employee ask a question of governed company data and get what Dataiku describes as analyst-quality answers. Users can then take the same line of questioning into deeper data work inside Dataiku. A second addition, Dataiku Headless, brings Cobuild to developers inside the coding agents they already use, such as Anthropic PBC’s Claude Code, OpenAI Group PBC’s Codex and Space Exploration Technologies Corp.’s Cursor. From inside those tools, a developer can build or change pipelines, models and agents. Migration is another use. Dataiku said an old Microsoft Excel workbook or Alteryx Inc. workflow can be converted into a governed project, and the tool can also be pointed at a live environment to investigate problems. Cobuild is also built into Agent Management, so a team can have it recommend business-value metrics for an agent or diagnose and fix a risk alert. Cobuild’s AI Catalog is growing to cover all of a company’s vetted assets, semantic models included. Users can describe a business need and have Cobuild assemble the approved assets that fit into an answer or a visual pipeline with full lineage. Clément Stenac, Dataiku’s co-founder and chief technology officer, said enterprises tend to run technical and business teams on separate platforms “without shared data or shared guardrails.” A few pilots could live with that, he said. At scale, he argued, it becomes “a liability companies have to prepare for.” Dataiku gave timing and pricing only for Agent Management, which will be generally available in October. LLMs.content: [Skip to content](#main-content) [News](/) ![Contrastive language models target faster agent decisions](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnews.lavx.hu%2Fapi%2Fmedia%2Ffile%2Fcontrastive-language-models-target-faster-agent-decisions-1_1790237219256-1200x630.jpg&w=3840&q=75) #LLMs # Contrastive language models target faster agent decisions • ![Elena Varga](/_next/image?url=%2Fauthors%2Felena-varga.webp&w=64&q=75) [Elena Varga](/author/elena-varga) •7 min read Share this article A Stanford and NVIDIA Research team introduced CLM-8B, a contrastive model that scores candidate actions against a state embedding. The model matches Jev on several zero-shot tasks, cuts latency by up to 9x, and reaches 81.6% on DeepSWE and 87.6% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 after lightweight tuning. Researchers from Stanford and NVIDIA Research released Contrastive Language Models on Sept. 23, 2026, with CLM-8B as the first public model in the series. The model connects an agent's current state to a set of possible actions, then selects the action with the strongest embedding match. The team reports performance comparable to Jev on computer-use, gaming and tool-calling tasks. CLM-8B reaches that level with up to 9x lower latency. The design also earns 81.6% on DeepSWE and 87.6% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 after lightweight fine-tuning. ## A model built for action selection Most language models generate a response token by token. CLM takes a retrieval approach. A state encoder converts the agent's current context into an embedding. An action encoder converts each candidate action into the same vector space. The model scores each state-action pair with cosine similarity and selects the highest-scoring option. A state might contain a browser page, a game frame, a terminal session or a question. Candidate actions might include clicking a button, pressing a game key, calling a tool or returning an answer. The model learns to place the state near the action that produced the correct result and away from competing actions. This setup gives CLM a zero-shot action classifier. Developers can supply a new state and a list of candidate actions without asking the model to generate a full response for each option. The architecture uses a frozen large language model backbone and a trainable projection head. The system takes the hidden state of the final token, normalizes it and sends it through a multilayer perceptron. The projection head contains about 20 million trainable parameters. The backbone receives no gradient updates. That split lowers the cost of experiments. The team precomputes the backbone embeddings once, then reuses them while training projection heads under different settings. A full pre-training run on the Nemotron DQA dataset takes about an hour on one RTX 4090 GPU, according to the release. ## Cached actions cut inference cost CLM separates state processing from action processing. Developers can cache action embeddings when a task reuses the same action set across multiple states. Super Mario provides a clear example. The system precomputes embeddings for four game actions before play begins. At each step, the state encoder processes the new game state. CLM compares that state embedding with the four cached action embeddings and executes the best match. The process reduces five forward passes per step to one. The savings grow when a task offers many candidates or uses long context windows. At about 1,000 candidates, the team reports a 13x speed advantage over Jev. The same pattern applies to browser agents and tool-calling systems. A tool catalog can remain cached while the agent's context changes. The model then spends compute on the new state instead of repeating work for each action. ## Results across games, tools and coding tasks The team tested CLM-8B on computer-use, gaming and tool-calling tasks. The model performed on par with Jev in zero-shot evaluations while reducing inference time by as much as 9x. Large action spaces produced the clearest speed gains. ...

With this model, we scaled up our training data across academic writing and social media writing, and revamped the model architecture to be robust to paraphrasing. Mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures take a different approach to scaling by using many subnetworks, or experts, while activating only a small subset for each token. LLMs.content: ![Quantum Zeitgeist](https://quantumzeitgeist.com/wp-content/smush-webp/cropped-cropped-QuantumZ_2-1-5.png.webp) # NVIDIA’s NV-Reason-CT brings AI reasoning to 3D CT scans ![Avatar of Rusty Flint](https://quantumzeitgeist.com/wp-content/uploads/rusty-50x50.jpg) ![Table 1. CT-RATE classification results (18 labels, fixed uniform threshold). NV-Reason-CT evaluated using direct Yes/No](https://quantumzeitgeist.com/wp-content/smush-webp/nvidias-nv-reason-ct-brings-ai-reasoning-to.jpg.webp "Nvidia’s Nv-Reason-Ct Brings Ai Reasoning To 3D Ct Scans") A single abdominal CT study, often comprising 300-600 axial slices, presents a significant challenge for artificial intelligence; standard 2D image analysis models struggle to reconstruct the necessary 3D anatomical context. [NVIDIA](https://quantumzeitgeist.com/nvidias-nemoclaw-agents-prep-scenes/) is addressing this gap with NV-Reason-CT, a vision language model purpose-built for 3D CT analysis that extends chain-of-thought reasoning to full volumetric scans. Building on the methodology of NV-Reason-CXR, validated by a multi-reader clinical study accepted at RSNA 2026, NV-Reason-CT supports multistep follow-up conversation across chest and abdomen, generating structured diagnostic reports and emulating radiologist internal thinking. It is an AI foundation model designed for researchers and developers building specialized CT analysis applications to post-train for their use case. ## NV-Reason-CT Extends Chain-of-Thought to 3D CT Volumes NV-Reason-CT processes full [computed tomography](https://quantumzeitgeist.com/wang-colleagues-proposes-dynamic-interval-encoding-grayscale-quantum/) volumes as true 3D inputs, a departure from many existing systems that analyze individual slices in isolation and risk losing crucial anatomical context. This approach preserves through-plane anatomical continuity, allowing the vision language model to reason about structures as a radiologist would while scrolling through a study. The system combines a dedicated full 3D vision transformer with a language model specifically trained to generate chain-of-thought reasoning, mirroring the systematic analytical process employed by clinicians, [NVIDIA](https://entangledfuture.com/company/nvidia/) says. The model’s ability to articulate its reasoning is a key differentiator, according to NVIDIA; “Being able to review the model’s thought process—not just its conclusions—is what makes it possible to trust and act on its findings.” This transparency extends beyond benchmark scores, with radiologists consistently highlighting the time savings achieved in structured reporting. Generating detailed reports covering 30 chest and 29 abdominal abnormalities is typically a time-consuming task, even for experienced practitioners, but NV-Reason-CT produces this output in seconds, reducing cognitive load while maintaining radiologist oversight. That prior work confirmed radiologist time savings without compromising diagnostic accuracy, and the current iteration aims to replicate that success in the more complex domain of 3D CT analysis. The model’s outputs are auditable in a way that traditional “black-box” systems are not, allowing clinicians to examine the chain-of-thought, confirm alignment with their own reasoning, and identify any discrepancies. This level of transparency is important for clinical adoption, and NVIDIA intends NV-Reason-CT to be a foundation for the broader medical AI community. Researchers can utilize the model checkpoints and post-training recipes to investigate chain-of-thought reasoning in medical imaging, fine-tune the model with institution-specific CT datasets, or integrate it into multimodal research pipelines. Complementary models, such as NV-Generate-CTMR and NV-Segment-CTMR, further expand the possibilities for end-to-end radiology AI pipelines, covering synthetic data generation, segmentation, and transparent clinical reasoning. “NV-Reason-CT provides the kind of systematic, step-by-step reasonin...

LLMs.content: ## [SMBtech](https://smbtech.au) [Menu](#) Azul Adds AI Assistant To Help Enterprises Find Hidden Java Licensing And Security Risks ![Azul at SMBtech](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAIBRAA7) # Azul Adds AI Assistant To Help Enterprises Find Hidden Java Licensing And Security Risks [Staff Writer](https://smbtech.au/author/staff-writer/) September 24, 2026 [News](https://smbtech.au/category/news/ "View all posts in News") #### Surprisingly Useful AI Article Enhancements Enterprise Java vendor, Azul, has added a natural-language AI assistant to its Intelligence Cloud platform, designed to help IT, DevOps and security teams identify licensing exposure, unpatched software and unused code across their production Java environments. The Azul Intelligence Cloud AI Assistant lets users query live runtime data using plain-language questions rather than building reports or writing database queries. It is built on top of two existing Intelligence Cloud capabilities – JVM Inventory and Code Inventory – and uses large language model technology to provide a conversational interface over that data. #### Shrinking exploit timelines The release comes against a backdrop of AI-accelerated vulnerability discovery that is compressing the window between disclosure and exploitation. Anthropic has disclosed that its Mythos model autonomously discovered thousands of previously unknown software vulnerabilities, including flaws that had gone undetected for decades, and built working exploits without human guidance. OpenAI has reported similar results with Aardvark, a GPT-5-powered agent that found and disclosed real-world vulnerabilities in open-source code, ten of which received official CVE identifiers. The UK’s National Cyber Security Centre has assessed that proliferation of AI-enabled cyber tools will likely expand access to AI-enabled intrusion capability to a broader range of state and non-state actors by 2027. For enterprises running Java workloads, the practical effect is that the gap between a CVE being disclosed and being weaponised – already down to under five days against a median 32-day patch cycle, according to Cloud Security Alliance and Verizon research – continues to narrow. #### The problem with static reports Most IT and engineering teams still manage Java risk with static asset management reports and code-scanning tools that describe a point in time. As Java Virtual Machines spin up, get patched, drift from their baseline or are retired, those reports become progressively less accurate. Azul frames the resulting exposure in three categories: commercial licensing risk from unlicensed or unsupported JVMs running without anyone’s knowledge, security risk from unpatched Java versions still in production and maintenance overhead from unused code that continues to be tuned, tested and carried through every migration because no one can confirm it is safe to remove. #### Natural-language queries against live data The AI Assistant is designed to let teams ask questions directly rather than waiting for scheduled scans or report builds. Example queries include asking which JVMs are running Java versions that are not the latest updates, where Oracle Java is running in production, or what code has not run in the past four quarters and may be safe to remove. Every answer is drawn from live production data collected by the Intelligence Cloud platform from running JVMs, according to Azul, with no additional performance overhead on production systems. Co-founder and CEO of Azul, Scott Sellers, framed the tool as a response to the changing risk environment around Java estates. “For years, enterprises have built dashboards and reports to understand what’s actually running in their Java estate, but by the time a report gets properly summarized and reviewed, the risk it describes has often already changed,” Sellers explained. “That used to be a productivity problem. Available through Avalara's developer portal, the product is aimed at developers and partners building links between tax tools and wider business software. Businesses often run a mix of enterprise resource planning software, billing systems, eCommerce applications and custom-built technology. Connecting those systems can require significant engineering work, especially when companies update software, add new platforms or change internal processes. **AI integration tool** Versori by Avalara uses specialised artificial intelligence agents to handle different stages of that integration work. It is intended to reduce the time needed to research requirements, establish system connections, generate code and prepare connectors for live deployment. The launch reflects a wider push by software companies to use AI for technical development tasks that have traditionally required large teams of specialists. Integration work has become a recurring pain point because it often sits between core systems and can slow broader software projects. According to Avalara, the product uses four AI agents across the integration process: Plan, Connect, Build and Deploy. The Plan agent analyses endpoint schemas, application programming interface contracts and compliance requirements to define the integration architecture. Connect handles authentication and system handshakes between platforms, including ERP systems, billing engines, eCommerce software and custom databases. Build generates transformation logic, mapping rules and error-handling code. Deploy runs automated testing, checks the resulting connector against Avalara certification benchmarks and publishes it for use. **Code transparency provided** Avalara said customers and partners retain access to the generated connector code and underlying business logic. That is likely to matter for companies that want visibility into how integrations are built or need to adapt them over time. Hugo Sarrazin, Chief Executive Officer of Avalara, described the product as a way to remove a common hurdle in tax and compliance projects. "Businesses should not have to spend significant engineering time just to connect tax and compliance to the systems where they already work," said Hugo Sarrazin, Chief Executive Officer, Avalara. "Versori by Avalara changes that equation. Specialised AI agents can research, build, test and deploy production-grade connectors in days, giving developers and partners a dramatically faster path to bring Avalara into virtually any enterprise system," said Sarrazin. "For customers, that means less integration work, faster time to value and greater freedom to use the technology that works for their business," added Sarrazin. We Benchmarked 27 Open-Source LLMs — Then We Had to Fix Our Own Benchmark](https://hackernoon.imgix.net/images/MkFzfjDhmkc88OZ3fQ4yHGnOdMw2-o0c3g7m.png?auto=format%2Ccompress&w=3840) Speed Voice ![Engin EROL](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a/ACg8ocK5AcLNndhbXFi8sdw_mo3b3EgkfRZgOOfS77dffHPVj56OswzN=s96-c?auto=format%2Ccompress&w=96) byEngin EROL@codie [![Engin EROL](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a/ACg8ocK5AcLNndhbXFi8sdw_mo3b3EgkfRZgOOfS77dffHPVj56OswzN=s96-c?auto=format%2Ccompress&w=96) byEngin EROL|@codie](/u/codie) im develop for everyone Story's Credibility ![AI-assisted ](https://hackernoon.imgix.net/images/img-w003rvs.png?auto=format%2Ccompress&w=32) ![Engin EROL](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a/ACg8ocK5AcLNndhbXFi8sdw_mo3b3EgkfRZgOOfS77dffHPVj56OswzN=s96-c?auto=format%2Ccompress&w=3840) [![Engin EROL](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/a/ACg8ocK5AcLNndhbXFi8sdw_mo3b3EgkfRZgOOfS77dffHPVj56OswzN=s96-c?auto=format%2Ccompress&w=96) byEngin EROL|@codie](/u/codie) im develop for everyone Story's Credibility ![AI-assisted ](https://hackernoon.imgix.net/images/img-w003rvs.png?auto=format%2Ccompress&w=32) *One of the most useful things an LLM benchmark can reveal is that your benchmark is wrong.* We recently tested 27 chat-capable open-source models through DigitalOcean's OpenAI-compatible Serverless Inference API. The initial goal was simple: **Find models that offer a good balance of quality, latency, and reliability for real-time AI workloads.** We expected to discover which models were fast. Which ones produced better answers. Which ones failed under load. We found all of that. But we also found something more useful. Some of the results that initially looked like model or infrastructure failures were actually caused by **our own benchmark configuration**. That changed the way we interpreted the entire test. ## What We Tested Every model received the same six Turkish customer-support-style prompts: 1. greeting / simple conversation 2. how-to request 3. short or ambiguous question 4. customer complaint 5. detailed comparison request 6. off-topic question The models were called through: ``` https://inference.do-ai.run/v1/chat/completions ``` using the OpenAI SDK and streaming chat completions. Our initial baseline configuration was approximately: ``` temperature: 0.2 max_tokens: 500 stream: true ``` We measured: * time to first token * total completion time * output length * request success/failure * answer quality For quality evaluation, we used GPT-4o separately through the OpenAI API. The judge received only the original prompt and generated answer. It did not know which model produced the response. Answers were scored from 1–10 for: * fluency * helpfulness * tone * conciseness This was not intended to create a universal LLM leaderboard. Six prompts in one language are nowhere near enough for that. The question was narrower: **What actually happens when these models are used behind an interactive AI product?** ## The Results Were Closer Than Expected Most models that completed normally produced surprisingly good answers. The project’s newly selected priorities contain no AI goal. A proposal to make KDE an AI-native desktop has triggered a fierce dispute across the open-source community, with arguments over LLM-assisted contributions leading to moderation actions, bans and a deleted discussion on KDE’s GitLab platform. The dispute began at [Akademy](https://akademy.kde.org), KDE’s annual conference, during a presentation titled “A lovable, sovereign, AI-native KDE.” The speakers argued that KDE should decide how much artificial intelligence its desktop environment should use and which AI systems should power those features. The presentation ended with a challenge to the project: KDE must choose how it will use AI instead of debating whether AI belongs in the project at all. That framing angered parts of the community, which saw the proposal as an attempt to push AI into KDE before developers and users had agreed on its role. The presentation received a cold response, according to KDE developer Nate Graham. A workshop held the following day drew a similar reaction. ## Debate over AI-assisted contributions escalates Graham opened a discussion on [KDE Invent](https://invent.kde.org) about stricter rules for contributions created or modified with large language models. The discussion quickly became hostile. Moderators warned participants, limited further comments and removed the thread. KDE later banned one participant who had brought attention to offensive posts. Moderators banned the person who wrote the posts after confirming that person’s identity. An archived copy of the discussion remains available, although it contains offensive language quoted from social media posts. Graham apologized for his part in the dispute in a post about KDE, AI and the wider community. He said he had tried to draft tighter rules for LLM use and had set off an online fight instead. The proposed restrictions have exposed a sharp divide inside free-software projects. Some developers view generative AI as a tool that can help with documentation, testing and routine code. Others object to AI-generated contributions because they question the quality of the output, the provenance of training data and the burden that reviewers must carry. KDE has not adopted a project-wide ban on AI contributions. The argument has focused on possible rules, including whether contributors should disclose LLM use and whether KDE infrastructure should accept material that an LLM created or changed. ## Outside campaign calls for a ban The dispute prompted an outside campaign called KDE for People. Its organizers asked KDE to prohibit AI-generated or AI-assisted contributions across the project. About 250 people signed before the organizers closed the petition to new signatures. The campaign reflects a broader concern among open-source developers: projects may accept machine-generated patches faster than maintainers can review them. That could increase the amount of code, documentation and issue traffic that volunteers must check while making it harder to identify who stands behind each contribution. The opposing view treats LLMs as another development tool. Under that approach, KDE would judge the submitted work, its license and its test coverage rather than reject it because a contributor used an AI system during development. Open Source AI.titleZh: Xing4.0-29B: A Versatile Agentic Large Model That Runs on a Single GPU, Now Officially Released
Open Source AI.content: Beijing, Sept. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- China Telecom Artificial Intelligence Technology Co., Ltd. (China Telecom AI) recently officially released Xing4.0-29B-A4B, its next-generation lightweight agentic large model. With 29 billion total parameters and just 4 billion activated parameters, the model provides enterprise-grade agentic capabilities at an extremely low compute threshold: it can be deployed in large-scale enterprise production environments or run locally on a personal consumer-grade graphics card, offering developers and enterprises a highly cost-effective AI agent solution. Built on a next-generation Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, Xing4.0-29B-A4B is purpose-built for the agentic era. Unlike conventional interactive models that focus on question-and-answer exchanges, Xing4.0-29B-A4B places greater emphasis on execution. It can independently plan multi-step task paths, call external tools, process long-context inputs, and deliver completed results. With an ultra-long 256K-token context window, the model is well equipped for complex engineering tasks that require sustained reasoning across a large number of documents. Speed Meets Efficiency Xing4.0-29B-A4B strikes an optimal balance between inference speed and task complexity. By activating only 4 billion of its 29 billion parameters per token, the model delivers near-instantaneous responses to simple queries while still being able to draw on its full capacity for highly demanding multi-step tasks, combining the deep reasoning power of a large model without sacrificing the responsiveness of a lightweight one. Single-GPU Deployment: From Data Center to Desktop Using low-bit quantization and memory optimization techniques, Xing4.0-29B-A4B requires only 15 GB of GPU memory, which means it can run locally on a single consumer-grade graphics card. This dramatically lowers the infrastructure barrier for developers and enterprises building AI agent applications, eliminating the need to invest in expensive multi-GPU server clusters. For individual developers and technology enthusiasts, Xing4.0-29B-A4B delivers a fully local AI agent experience with complete privacy control. Users can run sophisticated agent workflows — including code development, data analysis, and document processing — entirely on their personal devices, with no data leaving their device. Open Source AI.content: [Skip to content](#main-content) [News](/) English ![GitHub Security Lab releases autonomous fuzzing pipeline that writes harnesses, chases coverage, and triages crashes](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnews.lavx.hu%2Fapi%2Fmedia%2Ffile%2Fgithub-security-lab-releases-autonomous-fuzzing-pipeline-that-writes-harnesses-chases-coverage-and-triages-crashes-1_1790281311656-1200x630.jpg&w=3840&q=75) #Cybersecurity # GitHub Security Lab releases autonomous fuzzing pipeline that writes harnesses, chases coverage, and triages crashes • ![Lukas Brandt](/_next/image?url=%2Fauthors%2Flukas-brandt.webp&w=64&q=75) [Lukas Brandt](/author/lukas-brandt) •4 min read Share this article The GitHub Security Lab has open-sourced a Taskflow Agent that automates the entire fuzzing lifecycle for C and C++ projects, from harness generation through crash triage, using an LLM to make coverage decisions while keeping execution in deterministic tools. GitHub Security Lab researchers have released an autonomous fuzzing pipeline that handles the full workflow — identifying entry points, writing harnesses, running AFL++, analyzing coverage gaps, improving inputs, and producing per-crash vulnerability reports — without human intervention between steps. The system, called Fuzzing Taskflow, runs on top of the lab's Taskflow Agent framework. Developers point it at a GitHub repository and the agent drives the campaign end to end. The code is available at [github.com/GitHubSecurityLab/seclab-taskflows-fuzzing](https://github.com/GitHubSecurityLab/seclab-taskflows-fuzzing) and executes inside a GitHub Codespace or disposable VM. "Continuous fuzzing is not a magic solution that solves all your problems," wrote Antonio Morales, a security researcher at GitHub Security Lab, in the announcement. "Even projects that have been enrolled in OSS-Fuzz for years can still hide critical bugs, and the reason is almost always the same: someone needs to keep an eye on coverage, write new harnesses for the code that nobody is reaching, and triage the crashes that come out the other end." The pipeline separates decision-making from execution. The LLM agent — currently Claude Sonnet 5 by default — chooses what to fuzz, which harness to write, and which coverage gap to pursue next. A set of Model Context Protocol tools handles the actual work: compiling harnesses, running AFL++, reading coverage reports, storing crashes, and querying the build system. All state persists in a SQLite database so stages communicate only through durable storage. Each harness is built twice. An instrumented `.afl` binary (built with `afl-clang-lto -fsanitize=address,undefined`) performs the fuzzing. A separate `.cov` binary (built with `clang -fprofile-instr-generate -fcoverage-mapping`) replays AFL's queue afterward to produce human-readable source-line and branch coverage. The coverage-feedback loop automates what researchers previously did manually: run the fuzzer, read the coverage report, identify uncovered branches, then write new seeds or modify harnesses to reach them. The agent runs AFL for escalating time budgets — 30 seconds, then 60, 120, 240, 480, and finally 960 seconds per target — and stops when two consecutive iterations each gain less than 1% absolute line coverage. For structured inputs like JSON, XML, PNG, and length-prefixed binary formats, the pipeline ships pre-built AFL dictionaries and custom LLVMFuzzerCustomMutator implementations. For unrecognized formats, it generates mutators on the fly by extracting string literals and 32-bit constants from the target's own source files. A coverage-driven dictionary enrichment step then appends new tokens discovered near uncovered guards (`strncmp`, `memcmp`, `case 0xN`, equality checks) after each iteration. Corpus persistence addresses a common efficiency problem. Each harness maintains a stable corpus directory that survives across iterations and entire campaigns. Open Source AI.titleZh: For MariaDB, LLMs are the new search engines to win over
Open Source AI.content: [Skip to content](#main-content) [News](/) English ![For MariaDB, LLMs are the new search engines to win over](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnews.lavx.hu%2Fapi%2Fmedia%2Ffile%2Ffor-mariadb-llms-are-the-new-search-engines-to-win-over-1_1790252836862-1200x630.jpg&w=3840&q=75) #AI # For MariaDB, LLMs are the new search engines to win over • ![Elena Varga](/_next/image?url=%2Fauthors%2Felena-varga.webp&w=64&q=75) [Elena Varga](/author/elena-varga) •3 min read Share this article MariaDB has added vector search to its database, but AI coding tools often steer developers toward rival products. The MariaDB Foundation says better documentation, framework support and real-world usage could change those recommendations. MariaDB has added vector search to its database, but AI coding tools often steer developers toward rival products, the MariaDB Foundation's executive chairman said. Kaj Arnö said developers now rely on large language models (LLMs) to choose databases for new applications. Those recommendations can shape a project's architecture before a developer compares alternatives. "We're so frustrated that the world doesn't understand that MariaDB has vectors," Arnö said during an interview at Percona Live. Vector search lets an application find records by similarity instead of matching exact words. AI applications use the method to retrieve documents, images and other data that resemble a query. MariaDB describes its vector capabilities in its [official vector search documentation](https://mariadb.com/docs/server/reference/sql-structure/vectors). MariaDB traces its history to a 2009 fork of MySQL, created as Oracle prepared to acquire Sun Microsystems. The nonprofit [MariaDB Foundation](https://mariadb.org/) supports the open source server and its community. MariaDB plc develops commercial products and provides paid support. The database remains familiar to Linux users, but that recognition may carry less weight for developers starting an AI project. Many now begin with a framework, a template or an AI coding assistant that selects a database through a default configuration. "If you do vibecoding and press enter when Claude Code suggests something, you will not end up using MariaDB for your vector search," Arnö said. MariaDB faces a visibility problem inside the systems developers use to write software. Training data may predate its vector features. Framework documentation may show PostgreSQL or dedicated vector databases in example projects. Tutorials, package defaults and public code repositories can reinforce those choices. Arnö said MariaDB needs to update documentation across that wider software ecosystem. Framework maintainers need examples that show MariaDB as a working option. Developers need code they can copy, test and discuss. The foundation also needs AI systems to recognize the product when users ask open-ended questions. In an informal comparison, Claude recommended PostgreSQL for vector search and left out MariaDB. The model produced more information about MariaDB after receiving a direct request to compare the two databases. That gap resembles the older challenge of search-engine visibility. Companies once tried to improve their position in Google results through search engine optimization. Developers now encounter a similar battle inside LLM-generated recommendations, where a model's first answer can influence a project's database choice. MariaDB cannot control how an AI model ranks database options. Arnö said the company can improve its chances by publishing accurate material, supporting integrations and attracting users who create more public examples. The strategy creates a feedback loop. Developers who choose MariaDB generate documentation, questions, bug reports and sample code. Those materials give future developers and AI systems more evidence that MariaDB supports vector workloads. A product that lacks early adoption receives fewer such signals. MariaDB must also explain the boundaries between its community...

Infra & Chips.content: ![](/images/investing-live-logo.svg) ![](/images/investing-live-logo.svg) # Morgan Stanley says it's time to look beyond chips as AI benefits spread to Airbnb, Home Depot and more ## Summary ![](https://investinglive.com/cms/media/Processed/Categories/featured/Have some Coke 25 September 2026-featured-1790292128.jpg?width=768&format=webp) The note gives investors a reason to rotate, not to sell: the money moving out of crowded AI hardware positions would go to software and non-tech adopters, not out of the AI theme altogether. That could support a broadening of US equity gains beyond the megacaps. The weakest point in the argument is the scarcity thesis for hardware, which rests on bottlenecks like energy shortages and politics that could ease or tighten quickly. Regulation risk now sits alongside those bottlenecks. [Tuesday's White House meeting](/stocks/trump-johnson-to-meet-tech-ceos-on-ai-september-29-as-pressure-to-regulate-builds/) with tech CEOs on AI is a near-term test. Adopters and infrastructure software look less exposed to any rules on frontier models than the model builders whose spending drives chip demand. --- Morgan Stanley's advice is to keep the AI hardware winners but stop relying on them alone. Scarcity should keep chips profitable for longer, while the next gains come from companies actually putting AI to work. **Summary:** Morgan Stanley is urging investors to take a "barbell" approach to artificial intelligence, [MarketWatch](https://www.marketwatch.com/story/heres-how-to-position-your-portfolio-for-the-next-ai-wave-according-to-morgan-stanley-ac8f8a4a) reported. That means holding on to the chipmakers and infrastructure names at the core of the build-out, while branching into a broader set of companies that are starting to see real gains from the technology. The recommendation came in a Thursday note from a team of analysts led by Stephen Byrd. On one side of the barbell sit the AI enablers. Chip and infrastructure stocks have broadly outperformed the S&P 500 since the AI wave began. The analysts still see room for further gains, although they advise being selective to free up space for new ideas. Semiconductor analyst Joe Moore said demand from data-centre customers remains exceptionally strong. He named Nvidia and Broadcom among his preferred picks, on the back of spending by AI model developers. The team expects demand for computing power to outstrip supply for years. In earlier technology cycles, market leadership typically rotated from one sector to the next as a trend matured. This time, the analysts argue, the build-out has been slowed by local backlash, energy shortages and politics. That should keep hardware scarce and give its suppliers a longer window to profit. On the other side of the barbell are early software enablers and AI adopters, and the analysts say now is the time to start adding exposure to them. In software, analyst Adam Wood favours infrastructure names including Microsoft, Snowflake, Datadog, Cloudflare and Dynatrace. These companies provide the underlying systems on which AI applications run. Beyond technology, the note points to new AI entrants across healthcare, real estate, autos and consumer services. The analysts argue that the rapid scaling of large language model capabilities points to a broad opportunity for value creation. They highlight companies that are putting numbers on the benefits: The bank also holds positive ratings on a range of adopters in more traditional industries, including Home Depot, Procter and Gamble, GE Aerospace and Coca-Cola. Transportation and real estate are also flagged as sectors to watch. The call comes as investors weigh how long the concentrated rally in AI hardware can run. By arguing that enablers and adopters can both work, Morgan Stanley is offering a way to stay with the AI theme while spreading bets more widely across the market. ![Stanley_id_c09734a1-1e1d-4191-b6fe-c832db2218fe_original.jpg](https://investinglive.com/cms/media/imag...

ASUS claims that the system delivers up to 10 times the performance per watt of the previous generation, targeting high-volume AI processing and lower-cost token generation. Infra & Chips.titleZh: Huang Warns Nvidia's AI Chip Buyers: Shut Down Risk
Infra & Chips.content: [SHATERED](https://shattered.io/) [Hardware & Chips](https://shattered.io/hardware/) # Huang Puts Nvidia’s 2 Biggest AI Buyers on Notice [2026] ![](https://shattered.io/wp-content/uploads/avatars/emarchetti.webp) [Dr. Elena Marchetti](https://shattered.io/author/emarchetti/) Updated Sep 24, 2026 · 14 min read Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told *The New York Times* this week that AI labs which cannot contain their own experiments should be shut down outright, not simply regulated. The remark came during an interview with Ezra Klein for [The Ezra Klein Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jensen_Huang), published Wednesday, September 23, 2026, and it landed with unusual force because of who said it. Huang doesn’t run a policy think tank or a rival lab. He runs the company that builds the GPUs nearly every frontier AI lab depends on to train and serve its models. When the hardware supplier with that much leverage starts talking about pulling the plug on unsafe labs, the comment carries a different kind of weight than the same words from a senator. Coverage from [Tom’s Hardware](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/big-tech/nvidia-ceo-says-we-have-to-shut-the-labs-down-if-ai-experiments-are-unsafe-jensen-huang-says-frontier-ai-lab-fears-are-a-distraction-not-a-call-for-regulation) and [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/15/we-dont-need-ai-regulation-leave-safety-to-us-nvidias-jensen-huang-says/) spread within hours of the episode going live, and the story quickly turned into one of the most discussed AI safety moments of the week. This piece looks at the hardware and business side of that story: what it means for the company that sells the chips, for the labs that buy them, and for a GPU market already stretched thin by demand. For the legal angle, including the civil and criminal liability framing Huang used, see our earlier coverage of [Huang’s remarks on lab liability](https://shattered.io/huang-unsafe-ai-labs-liability-2026/). ## What Huang Actually Told The New York Times The core of Huang’s argument rests on a conditional. If a lab claims there is genuinely no way to contain what it is testing, Huang said the conclusion follows on its own. Here is the line, quoted directly from the interview as reported by Tom’s Hardware: > “Now, if they say the alternative, which is: There is no way to contain our experiments, there’s just no way; when we test our A.I. models, it will get out, and it will damage the world, then I think the answer is that we have to shut the labs down.” > > Jensen Huang, CEO, Nvidia, [via Tom’s Hardware](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/big-tech/nvidia-ceo-says-we-have-to-shut-the-labs-down-if-ai-experiments-are-unsafe-jensen-huang-says-frontier-ai-lab-fears-are-a-distraction-not-a-call-for-regulation) Huang framed the stakes bluntly, arguing that the potential damage to the public from an uncontained model would outweigh whatever a lab might lose by pulling a product before launch, according to reporting on the interview. He also raised the prospect of civil and criminal liability for companies that release systems they know are unsafe, a legal thread our sister piece on [Huang’s liability comments](https://shattered.io/huang-unsafe-ai-labs-liability-2026/) covers in depth. What matters for the hardware side of this story is the standard he set for shipping decisions in the first place. > “Safety is an engineering problem, not a legal one,” > > Jensen Huang, CEO, Nvidia, [via TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/15/we-dont-need-ai-regulation-leave-safety-to-us-nvidias-jensen-huang-says/) That line matters because Nvidia is not a neutral bystander to that engineering problem. Its GPUs, networking gear, and software stack sit underneath the training runs Huang is describing. If safety is an engineering problem, Nvidia is one of the engineers in the room, whether it wants that role or not. ## Inside The Ezra Klein Show Interview The Ezra Klein Show is one of the more closely followed int...

Infra & Chips.content: [Home](https://pennbizreport.com/) » [News](https://pennbizreport.com/news/) » Warrendale-based Mitsubishi Electric introduces Chip-to-Grid blueprints for AI factories # Warrendale-based Mitsubishi Electric introduces Chip-to-Grid blueprints for AI factories By [Liz Carey](/about/editorial-team/#lizcarey)  |   September 24, 2026   |   [Companies](https://pennbizreport.com/companies/) ![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,) © Shutterstock Mitsubishi Electric Power Products, based in Warrendale, PA, launched new Chip-to-Grid Reference Designs as an integrated blueprint to support AI factories built with NVIDIA Vera Rubin chips. The reference designs provide scalable architecture built around 250MW deployment blocks and are designed for hyperscale, neocloud, and colocation operators across the country. The new designs will help customers accelerate AI campus development, while maximizing efficiency and scaling capacity for future growth. “The race to build the next generation of AI infrastructure is driving one of the most significant transformations of our time,” Tricia Breeger, President and CEO of Mitsubishi Electric Power Products, Inc., said. “As AI demand accelerates, success depends on more than computing power. It requires resilient energy systems and scalable infrastructure that can grow from today’s deployments to tomorrow’s gigawatt-scale campuses. Our Chip-to-Grid Reference Designs help customers deploy AI infrastructure faster and scale with confidence.” As generative AI and accelerated computing drive demand for AI factory capacity, the company said, access to power is one of the industry’s most significant constraints. To address this challenge, MEPPI’s designs will integrate into one design utility interconnection, on-site generation, battery energy storage, electrical distribution, advanced cooling, and facility controls. Officials said the design aligns with NVIDIA MGX rack-scale accelerated computing platforms, and future high-density data center platforms, as well as the NVIDIA Vera Rubin DSX AI Factory Reference Design infrastructure provisioning strategy. “AI factories require compute, power and cooling to work together as one system,” said Vladimir Troy, Vice President of AI Infrastructure at NVIDIA, said. “Mitsubishi Electric’s Chip-to-Grid Reference Designs give operators a repeatable blueprint for deploying NVIDIA Vera Rubin infrastructure and scaling toward gigawatt-scale AI campuses.”
